problem: Outdoor VLN agents (Touchdown, map2seq) struggle to track which part of a long instruction is already completed. Prior work grounds language to vision but ignores the agent's own spatial position in that grounding.
motivation: Humans first work out where they are before planning a route. Outdoor VLN takes place in unseen environments with no global topology, so global localization is impossible; a local, block-level notion of position is feasible. Word-level grounding alone is also insufficient for long instructions.
key_idea: Before planning, the agent predicts its progress within the current street block (distance to the next intersection) and uses this spatial-aware state to ground the relevant sentences and tokens of the instruction, which then drive action selection.
insight: Explicit supervision of block-progress gives the largest gain within BAL: removing L_BAL drops TC by 4.3 points on map2seq and 2.6 on Touchdown, and block-level supervision beats a global-level locating loss (rows 4 vs 5). Hierarchical sentence-plus-token attention beats either one alone. Sentence-relevance supervision matters less than expected, since even without L_HSA the model stays competitive. The long-term turning angle helps only at a suitable K (K=3 is best).
method: Block-aware spatial locating (BAL): an LSTM (phi_1) encodes the previous action, ResNet visual feature, current turning angle g^c, long-term turning angle g^l (sum of the last K turning angles, K=3) and junction-type embedding into a state o_t. A ReLU linear layer gives the spatial-aware state o_t^p.

Block progress predictor: a sigmoid linear head predicts e_t in [0,1), the progress within the current block (0 = start node, 1 = next intersection). It is supervised by an MSE loss against the ground truth N_step/N_all.

Hierarchical semantic association (HSA): the instruction is split into sentences at periods and average-pooled into sentence embeddings. o_t^p queries them by multi-head cross-attention, and a relevance predictor outputs per-sentence scores r_t.

Fine-grained token mask: each sentence's score is repeated over its tokens to form a mask M_t that filters the token embeddings (I ⊙ M_t). o_t^p then attends the masked instruction, and the resulting textual feature attends the visual feature.

Action planning: an LSTM decoder (phi_2) takes the attended visual feature, attended text, o_t, o_t^p and a timestep embedding. Its output is combined with each action's turning angle to score [FORWARD, LEFT, RIGHT, STOP]. Trained with cross-entropy.
Losses: L = L_AP + L_BAL + L_HSA. L_HSA is a weighted BCE on sentence relevance, with pseudo-labels generated by template matching.

setting.backbone: ResNet (ImageNet-pretrained) image encoder + BiLSTM text encoder + LSTM state/action decoders, trained end-to-end
setting.training_data: Touchdown (9,326 samples, Google Street View NYC) and map2seq (7,672 samples) training splits; sentence-level pseudo-labels from template matching
setting.observation: Street View panoramic egocentric RGB, junction-type embedding and heading/turning angles
setting.action_space: Discrete on the panorama graph: FORWARD, LEFT, RIGHT, STOP
setting.simulator: Touchdown / map2seq Street View graph environments (NYC)
setting.privileged: none (training uses block-progress labels derived from the graph and template-matched sentence labels; neither is used at test time)

results: Loc4Plan sets a new state of the art on Touchdown and map2seq. On the unseen test split it beats ORAR by 3.3 TC on Touchdown (18.2 vs 14.9) and 4.8 TC on map2seq (35.1 vs 30.3). On Touchdown seen test it matches PM-VLN (32.9 vs 33.4 TC) without PM-VLN's extra ground-truth path information, and cuts SPD from 23.8 to 11.5. Gains are larger for longer instructions and more complex trajectories.
limitations: Block progress labels rely on the known graph structure (intersections) during training, and the sentence-level labels are template-matched pseudo-labels.
Only evaluated on the Touchdown and map2seq NYC Street View graphs with small LSTM models. Absolute unseen-scenario success remains low (18–35% TC).
PM-VLN is compared on seen Touchdown only. Baseline unseen/map2seq results were re-run by the authors from public code.
